trust_boundary: evaluate() judges supplied evidence (dicts/JSON) and can never establish native execution. native_verdict(live) takes ONLY the live in-process run object built by _run_native (after source/build admission, with the real NativeBackend and its counters; module-private witness, slots, backend type check) and computes the numeric evaluation itself from that run's own report, catalogue cases and full/partial scope; no caller-supplied evaluation can be associated with a run. A JSON round trip drops the stamp. This is correct internal evidence association against forged reports and fake backends, not a security claim against code that monkeypatches this module.
guards: before any MLX import: clean tracked+untracked src/scripts/tests/provenance, HEAD == --source-commit == MLX2_INTAKE_SOURCE_COMMIT, every bound file equal to its HEAD blob, installed MLX core/libmlx/metallib hashed
after import mlx.core and before any device query: the imported extension (mx.__file__) is the admitted file with the admitted bytes, and mx.__version__ equals the admitted package metadata

before every backend dispatch and after every case: git HEAD equals the admitted commit, src/scripts/tests/provenance is clean including untracked files, and the bound source and MLX file snapshots equal the admission exactly (missing, extra or malformed entries refuse); the run stops before the next dispatch otherwise
after the run: HEAD unchanged, tree clean, snapshots unchanged, candidate and mlx.core module paths are the admitted ones
backend.release() runs in a finally block for every case; a receipt is written only for a completed run (exclusive creation)

optional float32 SDPA diagnostic: if present it must be a full finite float32 array before any metric; absent only with an explicit 'omitted' scope; diagnostic only, no acceptance threshold; native float16 and host float64 stay mandatory
